questions.explanation: MPP is Massive Parallel Processing, where more than one processor works on a query in parallel.

questions.stem: How is a query executed in non-MPP mode?
options: Its different pieces of code run one by one in sequence
Its different pieces of code run in parallel on all processors
It is rejected unless it has a filter
It is split across multiple locations
It is cached and never re-run
questions.explanation: In non-MPP mode the different pieces of a query's code are executed one after another in sequence.

questions.stem: How much faster does MPP make query execution compared with one-by-one execution, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: It is no faster, only cheaper
questions.explanation: Executing the pieces of a query in parallel on all processors makes execution 100 times faster than sequential execution.

questions.stem: For which operations is MPP mostly used?
options: Reading and writing, mostly inserts, in parallel
questions.explanation: MPP is mostly used to read and write, mostly insert, in parallel across more than one processor.

questions.stem: Where may the multiple processors used by MPP be located?
options: Only in a single data centre
In a single node or across multiple nodes, in the same location or multiple locations
questions.explanation: MPP processors may run in a single node or across multiple nodes, in one location or many.

questions.stem: Which older class of computer ran in MPP mode but was too expensive for the mass community?
questions.explanation: Mainframes ran in MPP mode for decades but were too expensive for mass use.

questions.stem: Which organisation is said to have the biggest MPP architecture in place?
questions.explanation: Google is said to have the biggest MPP architecture; Facebook and others also helped make MPP famous.

questions.stem: Why was Hadoop described as groundbreaking for MPP?
options: Because it was the first cloud service
Because it ran only on mainframes
Because it was installable and usable on commodity hardware, even home laptops
questions.explanation: Hadoop made MPP installable and usable on community hardware, so everyone started using it, even on home laptops.

questions.stem: What does elastic cloud computing allow when a user runs a query?
options: The query is queued until the next day
The query is limited to one processor
The query is converted to MDX
The query must be pre-approved by procurement
Hundreds of nodes and processors can be spun up automatically within milliseconds if required
questions.explanation: Cloud elastic computing can automatically spin up hundreds of nodes and processors within milliseconds to serve a query.

questions.stem: How long may a report or dashboard take before it is considered unacceptable in the current era?
questions.explanation: The key phrase is that any report or dashboard taking more than 3 to 5 seconds is a 'no no' in the current era.
